d. Relationship of Planning Proposals to Randolph Master Plan: 
(1) Land Uses. The land uses proposed are in accord with the City's plans for the area and include the general land use proposals contained in the Community Renewal Plan and the Master Plan for the City of Richmond.
(2) Thoroughfares. Proposals made with regard to street pattern, at service and collector levels, take into consideration the City's major street plan for the area and recommend two changes in the traffic proposals for the neighborhood as proposed by the Richmond Metropolitan Authority.
e. The Possibility of Stimulating Undesirable Changes
The possibility of the Randolph Project's ability to stimulate undesirable changes in adjacent areas is minimal for at least two reasons:
(1) The physical location of the Randolph project allows little chance for catalytic action in neighboring densities. With the advent of the proposed Downtown Expressway the Randolph Area will become strongly defined on all sides. The only close physical community ties will exist with the Maymont Community, a single family detached community adjacent and paralleling the composition existing in the Randolph Project. No changes are planned or predicted for this area.
